the design of embedded systems should be based on a hierarchical, component-based architecture, where each component is a state machine, and that the design process is based on two steps: (1) system configuration and (2) component scheduling.

the design of embedded software should be based on: a) a clear separation between system structure and system behaviour (i.e. the system architecture should not be mixed with system functionality); b) a clear separation among the three basic software development tasks: specification of system behaviour, scheduling and execution of components, and generation of the system software; c) a clear separation of system functionality into a set of components that are executed in a predefined order, and a set of components whose execution is controlled by the system

(1) the system structure is specified using a hierarchical graph; (2) the system behaviour is specified as a set of concurrent processes; (3) component scheduling is based on the notion of a task graph; (4) execution of the system is based on the concept of an execution graph; (5) the framework is based on the idea of program generation.
